title: Anthropic to invest $100 million to train AI engineer talent
source_used: Business Insider; Anthropic announcement also read
key_facts: Anthropic announced Claude Frontier Academy on Friday 2 Oct 2026, backed by a $100 million commitment.
It aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers (FDEs) by the end of 2027.
First cohorts include engineers from Accenture, Bain, Capgemini, Deloitte, McKinsey, Morgan Stanley, Novo Nordisk and Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
Engineers do a multi-day in-person program led by Anthropic engineers, then a 12-week residency leading a real Claude project at their own organization.
The first certified engineers are expected in early 2027.
Cohorts run in San Francisco, New York and London; participation is by nomination.
Business Insider says forward-deployed engineers are becoming a prized role; a Draup analysis found such openings rose to 1,404 across five major consulting firms in the year to May.
quote_evidence: Anthropic is investing $100 million to train 10,000 engineers to help companies move AI projects from idea to production.
Those who pass then enter a 12-week residency, leading a real Claude project at their own organization.
The first engineers certified from the program are expected in early 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Companies say they lack people who can put AI to work inside a real business; Anthropic is paying to train them.
